sources.name: Trase
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 for charts, graphics, maps and other representations of the data. Commercial use requires contacting info@trase.earth; this atlas is non-commercial civic education, so the CC BY term applies.
sources.licence_evidence: Stated on each dataset page, e.g. trase.earth/open-data/datasets/supply-chains-brazil-soy.
sources.notes: 190 datasets. THE SUPPLY-CHAIN DATASETS ARE NOT MAPPABLE AS POINTS: supply-chains-<country>-<commodity> is trade flow between subnational regions, companies and destination countries — a graph, not a set of places, and geocoding it would invent locations. The mappable ones are the FACILITIES datasets Trase began publishing in 2025: slaughterhouses and meat processing in Brazil, palm oil mills in Indonesia carrying Universal Mill List ids, cocoa cooperatives in Cote d'Ivoire, and about 9,300 Brazilian soy silos and processing sites, many with stated ownership. Those are what this layer should carry. Note the soy facility set was identified by an AI vision workflow that Trase state is over 90% accurate — which means it is not a register and a share of it is wrong; carry that in the layer note. spatial-metrics-* datasets are municipality-level deforestation and emissions and would be a country or admin layer, not points.
sources.discovery: trase.earth/open-data is server-rendered and paginated (13 pages), with filters ?country=&commodity=&year=. Dataset slugs are readable from the listing, so discover.page_link() can find the current facilities datasets rather than pinning one. The per-dataset download URL has NOT been read yet — do that before writing the harvester.

sources.name: Allen Coral Atlas
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0
sources.licence_evidence: ows:AccessConstraints in the WFS 2.0.0 GetCapabilities reads 'CC BY 4.0'; ows:Fees reads 'NONE'.
sources.notes: Layer names read from the WFS GetCapabilities, which is where they are legible — the WMS one emits ~4,000 <CRS> entries and truncates before the FeatureTypeList. Only these two feature types exist. GetFeature offers application/json, DefaultCRS is EPSG:4326, CountDefault is 1,000,000. DECLARED EXTENT IS -32 to +32 DEGREES, not the 30N-30S recorded earlier. Benthic maps to 10 m depth, geomorphic to 15 m.

sources.name: PalmWatch
sources.licence: described by its publishers as a free and open-source data project; no SPDX identifier or terms page read yet
sources.notes: Inclusive Development International with the University of Chicago Data Science Institute. Over 2,000 geolocated crushing mills across 32 countries, scraped from the supply-chain disclosures of 13-15 consumer brands — so each mill carries which brands source from it, who owns and operates it, and its RSPO certification status. That is the rare thing here: it names buyers, not just sites. Each mill also has a CATCHMENT POLYGON, drawn at roughly 50 km radius adjusted by road network analysis, with 20 years of University of Maryland tree-cover loss overlaid inside it, and past and future deforestation scores derived from that. THE CATCHMENT IS A MODELLED SOURCING AREA, NOT A PROPERTY BOUNDARY, and the deforestation inside it is not attributed to the mill by measurement — if the catchments are drawn, that has to be stated, or the map asserts that a named company cleared a specific forest.
sources.discovery: Not yet resolved. The site is a client-rendered application, so the download path has to come from its runtime requests or from the project's source — it is described as open-source, so look for the repository first. Do not guess a path.

sources.name: Cerulean oil slicks (SkyTruth)
sources.licence: unchecked — SkyTruth Terms of Service not yet read
sources.access_evidence: Endpoint and parameters transcribed from notebooks/Cerulean API Guide.ipynb in SkyTruth/cerulean-cloud, which is the document skytruth.org/cerulean-api links to. The linked copy is a Colab behind a Google sign-in; the repo copy is the same notebook and is readable.
sources.notes: Sentinel-1 SAR detections, January 2023 to present. GEOMETRY IS MultiPolygon, so this cannot use the existing worker route's circle layer — app.js needs a fill/line branch first. SkyTruth's own caveats, for the layer note: it is not possible to identify oil from SAR alone, so every feature is a POTENTIAL slick; coverage is EEZs rather than high seas; and max_source_collated_score is only available about 72 hours after an event, so near-real-time queries use slick_confidence instead. Default limit is 10 if unspecified. NOTE: the guide's own bbox examples read west,north,east,south (10.9,42.3,19.7,36.1) — send standard OGC minx,miny,maxx,maxy and verify the returned extent on the first live call.

sources.name: Cerulean slick sources (SkyTruth)
sources.licence: unchecked — SkyTruth Terms of Service not yet read
sources.access_evidence: Endpoint and parameters transcribed from notebooks/Cerulean API Guide.ipynb in SkyTruth/cerulean-cloud, which is the document skytruth.org/cerulean-api links to. The linked copy is a Colab behind a Google sign-in; the repo copy is the same notebook and is readable.
sources.notes: The attribution side: vessels and offshore infrastructure Cerulean associates with a slick. source_type is VESSEL, INFRA, DARK or NATURAL; source_rank 1-3 orders the candidates; source_collated_score runs -5 to +5 and SkyTruth recommend treating >0 as credible. THIS LAYER NAMES PARTIES, which is rare among these sources and raises the cost of getting it wrong: a score is an estimated likelihood, not a finding, and the popup must say so. AIS identity lags up to 72 hours.

It declares NO LICENCE FILE, which defaults to all rights reserved — not a problem for self-use, but the upstream terms below travel with the data and are the ones that bind republication. 4,020 records observed. THE SOURCE BLURS BURIAL LOCATIONS BY DESIGN and this harvester must never undo it: `geo` takes the values exact (455), coarsened (2,580), area (938), admin (47), and `coarsened` is the ~5 km blur applied to anything that is itself a burial location. An earlier mapping did not know that word and let all 2,580 fall through to a solid located dot. Unknown geo values now fail safe to 'unknown'. Do not add geocoding to this source. Direction is separate from magnitude: 3,485 harm, 458 redress, 77 watch — a large repatriation is a large event, not a bad one.

_publish_blockers.issue: The dataforgoodfr/CarbonBombs repo declares no licence, which defaults to all rights reserved. The underlying GEM trackers are CC BY 4.0 and the project list is from Kuhne et al., Energy Policy.
_publish_blockers.decision: Proceeding with the build. Raise again before the map goes public.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: attribute GEM and Kuhne et al., or ask hellodataforgood@gmail.com

_publish_blockers.issue: The datasets/land-matrix mirror states two different licences for the same data: README.md says CC BY-SA 4.0, datapackage.json says CC BY-NC 4.0. Share-alike and non-commercial are different obligations and only one can be correct.
_publish_blockers.decision: Building against the stricter reading (isolated archive, non-commercial site). Resolve against Land Matrix's own terms before publishing.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: check landmatrix.org terms, or use their API directly rather than the mirror

_publish_blockers.issue: None of the five WelcomeToYourGalaxy repos carries a LICENSE file, so each defaults to all rights reserved. That is moot for using your own work, but the upstream licences travel with the data and are not all permissive.
_publish_blockers.decision: Building. Add a LICENSE to each repo, and record per-source terms, before any of this is republished.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: add LICENSE files; confirm the IPIS and kiln terms, which are the two with no stated licence anywhere

_publish_blockers.issue: Both carry OpenStreetMap-derived rows, which are ODbL 1.0 — share-alike. Mixing share-alike data into a combined archive propagates the obligation to everything it is combined with.
_publish_blockers.decision: local_projects is marked isolate:true so it builds as a standalone archive, the same treatment land_matrix gets. remains_records is NOT isolated yet: its OSM share is not separated in the source file, so whether the whole layer inherits ODbL is unresolved.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: split the OSM-derived remains rows by their `register` field, or isolate that layer too

_publish_blockers.issue: This layer names specific vessels and platforms as candidate sources of pollution. source_collated_score is an estimated likelihood on a -5 to +5 scale, not a finding, and SkyTruth state that slicks cannot be definitively identified as oil from SAR alone.
_publish_blockers.decision: Not built yet. When it is, the score, the rank and the potential wording all have to reach the popup, and the layer name must not read as an accusation.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: read SkyTruth's Terms of Service and mirror their own language

_publish_blockers.issue: Mill catchments are modelled sourcing areas at ~50 km adjusted by road network, and the deforestation figure is tree-cover loss falling inside that modelled area. Drawing the catchment next to an owner's name reads as an assertion that the named company cleared that forest, which is not what the method establishes.
_publish_blockers.decision: Not built yet. If catchments are drawn, the modelled basis has to be in the layer note and the popup, not a footnote.
_publish_blockers.resolve_by: read PalmWatch's own methodology page and mirror its wording
